      "text": "ReadPragmaInteger throwing would propagate and set database status to FAILED_LOAD instead of FAILED_VERIFY on verification failures",
      "quote": "Before, on `Verify()` failure (return `false`) `MakeSQLiteDatabase()` would have set `status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_VERIFY` and now (exception) it would set `status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_LOAD`. Is this ok?",

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "sqlite3_column_text can return nullptr, potentially causing undefined behavior when constructing a string without a null check",

      ],
      "other_replies": [],

      "status_by_id": "rc:2535566375",
      "status_by_quote": "Done, returns an empty string now."
    },
    {

      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "ignoring sqlite3_finalize return values in the destructor prevents signaling errors to callers",
      "quote": "Some of the callers of `sqlite3_finalize()` used to check its return value. Here in the destructor it is too late to signal an error to the caller... Ignoring the return value does not look good.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author explained sqlite3_finalize only repeats prior errors, accepted in vasild's ACK",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2535526914"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "r:3487577017",
      "status_by_quote": "ACK 0af7c2a11819a21e11abf34b4229c5c21150d827"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2646362930",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "initialize SQLiteStatement objects on first use rather than upfront in batch initialization",
      "quote": "I think it would be cheaper and less complicated to initialize statement objects just before they are used in the various `Read*()` `Erase*()` , and it takes better advantage of the fact that statemen",

      "status_note": "added commit to construct statement on first use",

        "rc:2658468710"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2658468710",
      "status_by_quote": "However, we can construct the `SQLiteStatement` on first use instead of always, so I've added a commit to do that."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3645464121",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "uncompiled trailing SQL is silently ignored when multiple statements are passed to sqlite3_prepare_v2 without checking pzTail",
      "quote": "provide the `pzTail` argument and throw an error if `pzTail` is not Null after `sqlite3_prepare_v2` (this indicates that there is uncompiled SQL code left)",
      "clears_with": "answer",

      "status_by_quote": ""

claims.quote: Before, on `Verify()` failure (return `false`) `MakeSQLiteDatabase()` would have set `status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_VERIFY` and now (exception) it would set `status = DatabaseStatus::FAILED_LOAD`. Is this ok?
claims.status_note: changed to catch exception and return std::nullopt
claims.status_by_quote: I've changed this to catch the exception and return `std::nullopt`.

claims.text: sqlite3_column_text can return nullptr, potentially causing undefined behavior when constructing a string without a null check
claims.quote: `sqlite3_column_text()` can return `nullptr`, better check that. The previous caller did check
claims.status_note: handled nullptr and returns empty string
claims.status_by_quote: Done, returns an empty string now.

claims.text: ignoring sqlite3_finalize return values in the destructor prevents signaling errors to callers
claims.quote: Some of the callers of `sqlite3_finalize()` used to check its return value. Here in the destructor it is too late to signal an error to the caller... Ignoring the return value does not look good.
claims.status_note: author explained sqlite3_finalize only repeats prior errors, accepted in vasild's ACK

claims.text: initialize SQLiteStatement objects on first use rather than upfront in batch initialization
claims.quote: I think it would be cheaper and less complicated to initialize statement objects just before they are used in the various `Read*()` `Erase*()` , and it takes better advantage of the fact that statemen
claims.status_note: added commit to construct statement on first use
claims.status_by_quote: However, we can construct the `SQLiteStatement` on first use instead of always, so I've added a commit to do that.

claims.text: uncompiled trailing SQL is silently ignored when multiple statements are passed to sqlite3_prepare_v2 without checking pzTail
claims.quote: provide the `pzTail` argument and throw an error if `pzTail` is not Null after `sqlite3_prepare_v2` (this indicates that there is uncompiled SQL code left)
claims.status_note: author deferred addressing this ("If I need to retouch"), leaving it open

claims.text: copying SQLiteStatement would cause double finalization of m_stmt and likely crash
claims.quote: A copy would double finalize `m_stmt` (I think that would crash).

claims.text: remove redundant static_cast and evaluate static_assert condition in Column template
claims.quote: I think the static_cast is a no-op. sqlite3_column_int64 already returns an int_64.
claims.status_note: author explained sqlite3_int64 is a typedef and cast ensures conversion to used type
claims.status_by_quote: It's a `sqlite3_int64` which is a typedef of `long long int`. The static cast is to put it into a type that we actually use.

claims.text: ExecEraseStatement is mentioned in the commit message as renaming ExecStatement, but is never defined in .cpp
claims.quote: You mention in the commit message that  ExecStatement is renamed to `ExecEraseStatement`, but this last is never defined in .cpp.

claims.text: why not use unsigned char directly for the span parameter
claims.quote: Is there any specific reason not to use `unsigned char` directly, like `std::span<const unsigned char > sp)` ?
claims.status_note: author explained uint256 value_type could theoretically change
claims.status_by_quote: In theory we could change `uint256`'s `value_type`, and we wouldn't need to make any changes here in that case.

claims.text: whether Bind should throw an exception instead of returning false since failure to bind cannot be recovered from
claims.quote: I wonder if `Bind` should throw an `Exception` instead? It doesn't look like we can recover from a failure to `sqlite3_bind_blob`.
claims.status_note: author explained not all callers have exception handling
claims.status_by_quote: Not all callers of this will have exception handling, but they all should have handling if it fails.
